entry.title: Org issue field cache classification has gaps (stale DATE fields, per-name init, status --update, field create)

fields.description: Code review of #932 found four places where the cached .gh-pmu.json field kind is wrong or incomplete, so the cached-metadata fallback can treat an org issue field as a project field. (1) checkCachedIssueFieldClassification (internal/api/fields_fallback.go:112-124) only refuses option-less single-selects with no kind; a pre-#932 cache entry for an issue-backed DATE field (e.g. Start date) passes. (2) init's per-name resolver fallback (cmd/init.go:318-336) never runs issue field classification, so fieldMetadataFromProjectField stamps kind PROJECT_FIELD on an issue-backed Priority, which also defeats the guard. (3) status --update (cmd/status.go:191-197) writes kind but not issue_field_id / issue_field_data_type. (4) field create (cmd/field.go:183-188) hard-codes PROJECT_FIELD.
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Keep a .gh-pmu.json written before #932 on an org board whose Start date is an org issue field.
2. Make the ProjectV2 fields resolver fail (5xx) so the cache fallback engages.
3. Set Start date on an issue.
fields.expectedBehavior: An unclassified or incomplete cache entry is refused with 'gh pmu init' as the remedy, and never routed to the project-field mutation.
fields.actualBehavior: The DATE entry passes the guard, loads with IssueField nil, and the write goes to updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue on the project projection.
fields.inScope: Cache guard for every unclassified (kind absent) entry; init per-name fallback leaving kind unset (or classifying); status --update and field create writing complete kind data.
acceptanceCriteria: A cached entry with no kind of any data type is refused by the fallback with an error naming 'gh pmu init' (unit test with a pre-#932 DATE fixture)
init's per-name fallback does not record kind PROJECT_FIELD for fields it could not classify (unit test)
status --update records issue_field_id and issue_field_data_type when Status is issue-backed (unit test)
field create records the created field's actual classification or leaves kind unset (unit test)
fields.proposedFix: Treat kind == "" as unclassified for every data type in checkCachedIssueFieldClassification; have the per-name init path write an empty kind; build status/field-create metadata through fieldMetadataFromProjectField.

entry.title: Org issue field reads drop TEXT/NUMBER/MULTI_SELECT values and the board can truncate Priority

fields.description: The ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue read selections (internal/api/fieldvalues.go typed and raw) select only IssueFieldSingleSelectValue.name and IssueFieldDateValue.value, so text, number and multi-select issue field values decode to an empty string and are dropped, while discovery still classifies those fields. Separately the board query uses fieldValues(first: 10) (internal/api/queries.go:1360-1409) with no pageInfo, so an org Priority value can fall outside the first 10 values and the board shows it empty.
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. On an org board, set a TEXT org issue field (Notes) on an issue, or populate 11+ field values on an item.
2. Run gh pmu view N, or gh pmu board.
fields.expectedBehavior: Every issue field value is shown, or its absence is reported; board Priority matches view.
fields.actualBehavior: Notes is missing from view; board shows an empty Priority while view shows P1.
fields.inScope: Read selections for all issue field value types; board fieldValues limit and truncation detection.
acceptanceCriteria: view/list/board surface TEXT, NUMBER and MULTI_SELECT issue field values (unit tests with mocked ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue responses)
The board query fetches at least as many field values as the other item queries and warns when values were truncated (unit test)
fields.proposedFix: Add IssueFieldTextValue, IssueFieldNumberValue and IssueFieldMultiSelectValue fragments to both selections and decode them; raise the board limit to 20 and select pageInfo.hasNextPage.

entry.title: Gate the issue field value fragment on schema support

fields.description: Since #932 every project item and field-value query includes '... on ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue' (typed via typedFieldValueNode and raw via rawIssueFieldValueSelection), for user-owned projects too. A GraphQL server whose schema lacks that type rejects the whole document, so view, list and board stop working there.
fields.motivation: The charter lists resilience to upstream GraphQL schema rollouts. Issue field discovery is already gated on org ownership; the read path is not, so a GitHub Enterprise Server host without the issue fields rollout loses all reads.
fields.proposedSolution: Include the fragment only when supported: gate on org ownership plus a one-time capability probe, or on a validation error naming ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue retry once without it and warn.
fields.inScope: Typed and raw item/field-value queries in internal/api/queries.go and fieldvalues.go.
acceptanceCriteria: When the server rejects ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue, view/list/board still return project field values and print one warning (unit test with a mocked validation error)
github.com behaviour is unchanged: issue field values are still read (existing #932 read tests pass)
Modified GraphQL documents pass offline schema validation

entry.title: Re-init and Config.Save drop config keys (issue_field overrides, configIntegrity, nested keys)

fields.description: writeConfigWithMetadata (cmd/init.go:707-767) rebuilds .gh-pmu.json from a fixed struct: it keeps issue_field overrides only for aliases it regenerates (status, priority, branch; cmd/init.go:717-723) and drops unmodeled top-level keys such as configIntegrity. Config.Save (internal/config/config.go:30-98) preserves unknown keys only at top level, so keys inside fields.<alias> or metadata.fields[] written by a newer build are lost when an older build saves.
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Add "configIntegrity": "strict" and fields.severity = {field: Severity, issue_field: none} to .gh-pmu.json.
2. Run gh pmu init --project N --repo o/r --yes.
fields.actualBehavior: configIntegrity and the severity alias with its override are removed.
fields.inScope: Re-init key preservation; nested unknown-key preservation in Config.Save.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-init preserves every existing fields.<alias> issue_field override (unit test)
Re-init preserves unmodeled top-level keys such as configIntegrity (unit test)
Config.Save preserves unknown keys inside fields.<alias> and metadata.fields[] entries, or the limitation is documented and warned about (unit test)
fields.proposedFix: Load the existing file through config.Config and merge regenerated sections into it; extend unknown-key capture to the nested structs.

entry.title: Raw batch GraphQL parsers ignore the errors array and report failures as empty or not found

fields.description: The raw GraphQL path (DoRawBody) only fails on non-200 status, so GitHub's HTTP 200 {errors: [...]} responses reach the parsers. getProjectFieldsForIssuesBatch (internal/api/queries.go:1983-2024) has no errors field and returns an empty map with a nil error; parseParentIssueBatchResponse (3073-3095) decodes errors but never reads them; parseIssuesBatchResponse (2930-2953) ignores errors whose path has fewer than 2 segments and reports every issue as 'not found'.
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Run gh pmu list / board / view 1 2 3 while rate-limited, or with a token lacking repo read.
2. The server returns 200 with an errors array.
fields.expectedBehavior: The command fails non-zero with GitHub's error message.
fields.actualBehavior: Issues show no field values, no parent, or 'issue #N not found', and the command exits 0.
fields.outOfScope: Typed shurcooL queries (they already surface errors).
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three parsers returns an error carrying GitHub's message when the response has a top-level or document-level errors entry (unit test per parser with a mocked 200 errors response)
Per-alias errors keep their current per-issue handling (existing tests pass)
fields.proposedFix: Decode errors in every raw response struct; return document-level and short-path errors as a top-level error, matching parseSubIssueCountsResponse.

entry.title: Partial failures exit 0 in branch close, view, field create, recursive move, sub create and init

fields.description: The charter requires a command that partly fails to exit non-zero. These paths print warnings and return nil: branch close moving incomplete issues (cmd/branch.go:1171-1236, also reports len(issuesToMove) as moved); multi-issue view (cmd/view.go:345-369, only errors when all fail); field create when the config update fails (cmd/field.go:176-205); recursive move when sub-issue enrichment fails (cmd/move.go:304-334, counted as skipped) or a subtree cannot be listed (cmd/move.go:772-793); sub create when adding to --project fails (cmd/sub.go:451-488); init when the post-setup field refetch fails (cmd/init_atomic.go:86-100, writes empty metadata).
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Run gh pmu view 42 999999.
2. Or gh pmu branch close --yes while one field write fails.
fields.expectedBehavior: Non-zero exit (partial-success exit code) naming what failed; reported counts reflect what actually happened.
fields.actualBehavior: Exit 0 with only stderr warnings; branch close reports every issue moved.
acceptanceCriteria: Each listed path returns a non-nil error (or api.PartialSuccessError) when any part failed (unit test per path)
branch close reports the number of issues actually moved
init keeps the earlier fetched fields when the refetch fails instead of writing empty metadata
fields.proposedFix: Track failures per path and return a partial-success error after completing the remaining work, following the create command's #929 pattern.

entry.title: Discarded fetch errors read as empty results in move, view and sub list

fields.description: Several fetches discard their error, so a failed call looks like an empty answer: move discards the GetOpenIssuesByLabel error (cmd/move.go:404-411), which empties activeReleases and disables branch validation (fail-open); view discards GetSubIssues, GetParentIssue and GetIssueComments errors (cmd/view.go:461-481 and the multi path); sub list discards parent and sibling fetch errors (cmd/sub.go:668-701).
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Cause a transient GraphQL error.
2. Run gh pmu move 42 --status in_progress --branch release/v9.9.9, or gh pmu view 10 --json=subProgress, or gh pmu sub list 15 --relation parent.
fields.expectedBehavior: The fetch error is reported and the command exits non-zero.
fields.actualBehavior: Validation passes for a non-existent branch; view prints no sub-issues; sub list reports no parent; all exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: move fails the transition (non-zero) when the active-branch fetch fails (unit test)
view and sub list return an error when a requested sub-issue, parent, sibling or comment fetch fails (unit tests)
fields.proposedFix: Propagate each error; distinguish 'fetch failed' from 'none exist'.

entry.title: move: an empty unchecked box (`- [ ]` with no text) no longer blocks in_review/done

fields.description: Since #923, Rule 2 in `cmd/validation.go` (around line 99) decides which lines block with `partitionUncheckedItems`. That function is built on `uncheckedItemRegex` (`^\s*[-*+] \[ \] (.+)`), which needs a space and at least one more character after the box. Before #923 the gate counted boxes with `uncheckedBoxRegex` (`^\s*[-*+] \[ \]`), which needs no text. So a bare `- [ ]`, or `- [ ]` followed by a tab, is now counted as neither blocking nor waived. The `--force` warning in `cmd/move.go` (around lines 436-444) undercounts the same way. Found by the v1.8.0 release diff review.
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Make an issue body that contains the line `- [ ]` with nothing after the box.
2. Leave `checkboxGateMarkers` unset.
3. Run `gh pmu move <n> --status in_review`.
fields.expectedBehavior: The move is refused with `Has 1 unchecked checkbox(es)`, as it was before #923.
fields.inScope: Rule 2 blocking count and the `--force` warning count in move
fields.outOfScope: Changing which gate-marker formats are recognized
acceptanceCriteria: A body containing a bare `- [ ]` line blocks a move to in_review/done when no markers are configured (unit test in `cmd/validation_test.go`)
A bare `- [ ]` line counts as blocking in the `--force` warning (unit test in `cmd/move_test.go`)
Existing gate-marker tests still pass
fields.proposedFix: In `partitionUncheckedItems`, match every line `uncheckedBoxRegex` matches and apply the marker test to its text, which may be empty. An empty item always counts as blocking.

entry.title: BatchAddSubIssues: don't give a child another alias's error message

fields.description: In `parseBatchAddSubIssuesResponse` (`internal/api/mutations.go`, around line 2392), an alias with no data and no path-scoped error of its own gets `response.Errors[0].Message`. That message can belong to a sibling alias. In `addSubIssuesBatch`, a borrowed 'duplicate' or 'only have one parent' message sends the child down the `GetParentIssue` path. The child can then be reported as already linked, or as already having a parent, when its real failure was something else. Found by the v1.8.0 release diff review (low).
fields.motivation: Each child in a multi-child `sub add` should be reported with its own outcome.
fields.proposedSolution: Fall back to `Errors[0]` only when that error has no path, meaning it applies to the whole request. When every error is scoped to another alias, report 'no sub-issue returned'.
fields.outOfScope: Changing how the batch is chunked
acceptanceCriteria: A unit test where one alias has a path-scoped error and another alias has neither data nor an error: the second alias reports 'no sub-issue returned', not the first alias's message
A request-level error with no path is still given to aliases that have no data

entry.title: create --dry-run with --project shows status/priority that the real run would leave unset

fields.description: With a `--project` override, `setCreateFields` skips any status or priority whose field or option doesn't exist on the target board, and reports it as unset. `printCreateDryRun` (`cmd/create.go`, around lines 381-409) doesn't make that check, so it prints the locally resolved values, config defaults included, as if they will be written. Found by the v1.8.0 release diff review (low).
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Pick a target project whose Priority field has no P2 option.
2. Run `gh pmu create --title t --repo other/repo --project other/7 --dry-run` with the config default priority `p2`.
fields.expectedBehavior: The dry run says priority will be left unset on the target board.
fields.actualBehavior: The dry run prints `Priority: P2 (config default)`.
fields.inScope: printCreateDryRun when the project is overridden
acceptanceCriteria: With an overridden project, the dry run prints `(will be left unset: <reason>)` for a status or priority the target board can't take (unit test)
Dry-run output without an override is unchanged
fields.proposedFix: When `targets.overridden` is true, call `unresolvableOnProject` in `printCreateDryRun` and print the reason instead of the value.

entry.title: move --dry-run prints gate waivers before the dry-run banner

fields.description: The report of accepted gate lines (`cmd/move.go`, around lines 466-472) prints whenever `gateWaivers` is non-empty, in dry runs too. In a dry run it appears before the 'Dry run - no changes will be made' banner, which reads as if the move was accepted. The `--force` warning next to it is guarded by `!opts.dryRun`. Found by the v1.8.0 release diff review (low).
fields.stepsToReproduce:
1. Configure `checkboxGateMarkers`.
2. Make an issue with an unchecked AC line that ends in a marker.
3. Run `gh pmu move <n> --status in_review --dry-run`.
fields.expectedBehavior: The waivers are shown as part of the dry-run output, after the banner.
fields.actualBehavior: The waivers print above the dry-run banner.
fields.inScope: Where move puts the waiver report in a dry run
acceptanceCriteria: In a dry run, the waiver report comes after the dry-run banner (unit test on output order)
Waiver output in a real run is unchanged
fields.proposedFix: Print the waivers after the banner in a dry run, or fold them into the per-issue validation results.

entry.title: ratelimit backoff overflows for large retry counts, giving a zero or negative delay

fields.description: `Limiter.backoff` (`internal/testutil/ratelimit/ratelimit.go`, around line 321) computes `BaseDelay << attempt` with no bound on `attempt`. `E2E_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` can be set to any non-negative value. With the 5s default base, the shift overflows past about 30 retries, and the resulting negative Duration slips past the `MaxDelay` cap (`d > MaxDelay` is false). `MaxDelay=0` turns the cap off entirely. The result is retrying without waiting. This is test-support code only. Found by the v1.8.0 release diff review (low).
fields.stepsToReproduce: Set `E2E_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES=40` and drive repeated rate-limited responses through `Limiter.Do`.
fields.expectedBehavior: Each delay is capped at MaxDelay and is never zero or negative.
fields.actualBehavior: Past about 30 retries the delay wraps to a negative or zero value.
fields.inScope: backoff computation and the MaxRetries validation in ConfigFromEnv
acceptanceCriteria: backoff never returns a value <= 0 for any attempt (unit test with attempt 64)
backoff is capped at MaxDelay whenever MaxDelay > 0
fields.proposedFix: Stop doubling once the delay would pass MaxDelay, or treat d <= 0 as an overflow and clamp it. Alternatively, bound MaxRetries in ConfigFromEnv.
